parsed_output.analysis: The specification requires a sub-machine CollisionAvoidanceSystem that is entered only on detection of a possible front-end, rear-end or pedestrian collision and that is decomposed into three orthogonal regions so the three collision-avoidance controls can be active concurrently. The PlantUML model defines CollisionAvoidanceSystem as a composite with three child states Frontend, RearEnd and Pedestrian, but the three children are modelled as mutually exclusive substates with no parallel/orthogonal decomposition. Entry to the sub-machine is unconditional and exit is modelled with a single Collision Avoided transition, while detection is modelled as an internal Idle -> Braking transition inside each child.

issues.issue: No orthogonal / parallel decomposition for the three collision avoidance controls
issues.reason: Specification states there are three regions in the diagram and that the orthogonal regions of the active mode allow for concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls. The model defines Frontend, RearEnd and Pedestrian as three nested substates of CollisionAvoidanceSystem without parallel/orthogonal composition, so only one of them can be active at a time and concurrent activation is not possible.
issues.where: state CollisionAvoidanceSystem { state "Frontend Collision Avoidance" as Frontend ... state "Rear-End Collision Avoidance" as RearEnd ... state "Pedestrian Collision Avoidance" as Pedestrian ... }

issues.issue: Sub-machine entry is unconditional instead of triggered by detection
issues.reason: Specification requires the sub-machine to become active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected. The model enters CollisionAvoidanceSystem from [*] with no trigger/guard, i.e., unconditionally.

issues.issue: Detection event is used internally to each region instead of to activate the sub-machine
issues.reason: Specification says activation of the sub-machine is conditioned on detection of a possible collision. In the model Collision Detected is an internal transition from Idle to Braking inside each region, so the sub-machine can be entered without detection and detection does not cause entry.
issues.where: Idle --> Braking : Collision Detected in Frontend, RearEnd and Pedestrian

issues.issue: Unmodelled / incorrect deactivation of the whole sub-machine
issues.reason: Specification does not define a deactivation condition for the sub-machine and requires concurrent operation of the three regions. The model provides a single exit transition from CollisionAvoidanceSystem to [*] on Collision Avoided, which would deactivate all three controls together and precludes independent / concurrent lifetimes of the regions.

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
